rubrics.justification: Generally recognizes a very poor-quality early blastocyst/compacting embryo with absent-poor ICM/TE, but overstates non-viability and adds features like granular cytoplasm/disorganization not clearly assessable from the image; also notes the score-text discrepancy appropriately.

Integrates young age, BMI, ovarian response, sperm parameters, endometrium, and DOR diagnosis with embryo quality reasonably well, though some inferences (e.g., hidden male factor/cytoplasmic maturity) are speculative.

Reasoning is mostly logical and internally consistent, with the low implantation estimate matching the poor morphology; minor issues include equating DD with near-certain non-viability and some speculative causal explanations.

Mostly consistent with Gardner grading concepts and standard counseling for poor-quality embryos, but calling the embryo non-viable/unsuitable for transfer is stronger than guideline-based morphology alone supports, and some recommendations (routine DNA fragmentation testing, protocol changes, supplements) are not strongly guideline-driven.

Provides clear counseling points and practical future-cycle considerations, including reassessing reserve and considering extended culture, though several suggestions are somewhat generic or speculative rather than tightly case-specific.
